proposal.utterance: What BFO type fits 'the legal rule enduring relation'?

entities.label: LegalRuleEnduringRelation
entities.rationale: A 'legal rule enduring relation' refers to the pattern or informational structure that constitutes how a legal rule persists through time by virtue of being concretely realized in successive bearers (documents, practices, institutions). This pattern can be copied or multiply instantiated and does not depend on a single bearer for its identity — the hallmark of a Generically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000031). It is not a Quality (BFO_0000019) because it is not a measurable property inhering in exactly one bearer; it is not a Role (BFO_0000023) because it is not externally grounded social function; it is not a Process (BFO_0000015) because it is not an occurrent unfolding in time. The existing class 'EnduringInstitutionalForm' (working:EnduringInstitutionalForm, BFO_0000031) is the closest existing class and could serve as a parent, or this new class could be typed directly under BFO_0000031 with EnduringInstitutionalForm as a parent to capture the more specific notion of a rule-level enduring relational structure.

relations.rationale: LegalRuleEnduringRelation is a more specific kind of EnduringInstitutionalForm, restricted to the relational structure grounding the persistence of a legal rule specifically, inheriting its GDC typing.

open_questions: Do you intend 'legal rule enduring relation' as (a) the abstract pattern/information structure encoding how a rule persists (best fit: GDC / BFO_0000031), (b) a specific dyadic ontological relation between a legal rule and its instantiation contexts (which would require an OWL object property, not a BFO entity), or (c) a quality of persistence inhering in a single legal institution (BFO_0000019)?
Should 'LegalRuleEnduringRelation' be a new class (kind of thing) or an individual token of an enduring relational pattern in some specific legal system?
Is this intended to be a subclass of the existing 'EnduringInstitutionalForm', or should it be typed directly under BFO_0000031 with a different parent?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'legal rule enduring relation' most naturally picks out the abstract, copyable informational or structural pattern by which a legal rule maintains its identity across time and across different physical or social instantiations — a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031). It is not an occurrent (no unfolding in time as a process), not a quality inhering in exactly one bearer, and not a role. The closest existing class is working:EnduringInstitutionalForm (already typed as BFO_0000031), so the proposed new class LegalRuleEnduringRelation is typed as rdfs:subClassOf EnduringInstitutionalForm. However, three open questions are raised because 'enduring relation' could also mean an OWL object property (not a BFO entity at all), or a quality of persistence (BFO_0000019), depending on the user's intent. No individuals are proposed pending clarification.
